title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the Committee's 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its position and planned actions. It emphasizes strengthening oversight, improving transparency, and ensuring AI systems used in public services meet ethical and regulatory guidelines.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting up rules and oversight to control how artificial intelligence is used in exams and qualifications. The goal is to keep assessments fair, accurate and transparent while preventing any misuse of AI.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted materials and evaluates the legal, economic, and societal implications of such use. It offers recommendations for policymakers to balance innovation with intellectual property protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, acknowledging the report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It outlines a plan to strengthen AI regulation, boost innovation, and ensure ethical and safe use of AI while maintaining the UK’s competitive edge.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the scope, duties, and processes for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence should be integrated into public standards, including how it will operate and what it will cover. It also provides frequently asked questions to clarify the committee’s objectives, membership, and decision‑making framework.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. In its submission, the organization outlines concerns and offers recommendations for how AI should be regulated and managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how AI technologies are reshaping the oversight of medical products, highlighting new requirements for safety, efficacy, and compliance. It applies the AI White Paper principles to help regulators, manufacturers, and stakeholders update their regulatory frameworks to keep pace with AI’s evolving impact.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to position the organisation as the world's most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI-enabled defence force for its size. It focuses on leveraging AI technologies to enhance operational capabilities, streamline processes, and maintain strategic leadership in defence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to use AI to improve services, safety, and efficiency. It also outlines strategies to identify and mitigate risks that could arise from deploying AI technologies in transport.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The document reports on how copyright-protected works are being used to train and improve AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It evaluates progress, challenges, and policy recommendations for balancing intellectual property rights with AI development.
